metadata.case_name: CHAN WAI NGA v. TAM CHI WAI AND ANOTHER

injuries.description: Wai-Nga suffered scalds to her right trunk, right upper limb, right lower limb, a small area of her left thigh and left forearm, all together equal to about 15 percent of her body surface area. Approximately 11% of Wai-Nga's body suffered second degree burns.
injuries.body_part: right trunk, right upper limb, right lower limb, left thigh, left forearm
source: Wai-Nga suffered scalds to her right trunk, right upper limb, right lower limb, a small area of her left thigh and left forearm, all together equal to about 15 percent of her body surface area. Approximately 11% of Wai-Nga's body suffered second degree burns.

manifestations.description: the scars were all well healed, soft and pliable
the plaintiff has permanent cosmetic disability due to colour discrepancy which is accentuated by mild hyperpigmentation of the junctional area between normal skin and pale scald scars.
Approximately 11% of Wai-Nga's body suffered second degree burns.
generalized anxiety, increased arousal and irritability after the accident
the accident does not appear to have a lasting psychological impact on Wai-Nga
as she grows up, she may become conscious of the scars and bother by them

treatments_received: treatment at Yaumatei Child Psychiatric Centre
